synonyms: Matricaria recutita L. (POWO urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:231986-1; GBIF 3103774; NCBI: synonym of 'Matricaria chamomilla var. recutita', taxid 127986)
taxa.taxonomy_note: POWO and GBIF treat M. recutita as a synonym of M. chamomilla. NCBI differs: it maps M. recutita to the variety M. chamomilla var. recutita (taxid 127986), not to the species (98504). NCBI taxid read from the NCBI Taxonomy checklist that GBIF mirrors (dataset fab88965-e69d-4491-a04d-e3198b626e52), because the NCBI pages could not be reached directly (browser rate-limited, E-utilities blocked by robots.txt). pregnancy_lactation.statement: EMA monograph: 'Safety during pregnancy and lactation has not been established' for most preparations (not for preparation a); NCCIH: little is known.
pregnancy_lactation.md: [EMA](#term:ema-hmpc) [monograph](#term:monograph): 'Safety during pregnancy and lactation has not been established' for most preparations (not for preparation a); NCCIH: little is known.

allergy.statement: Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to chamomile or other Asteraceae (Compositae); hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylactic shock reported; higher risk with ragweed, chrysanthemum, marigold or daisy allergy. Anthemis cotula contamination (sesquiterpene lactone anthecotulid) is a further allergy risk.
allergy.md: [Contraindicated](#term:contraindication) in hypersensitivity to chamomile or other [Asteraceae](#term:asteraceae) (Compositae); hypersensitivity reactions including [anaphylactic shock](#term:anaphylaxis) reported; higher risk with ragweed, chrysanthemum, marigold or daisy allergy. Anthemis cotula contamination ([sesquiterpene lactone](#term:sesquiterpene-lactone) anthecotulid) is a further allergy risk.

adverse_event_history.statement: Severe allergic reactions (dyspnoea, angioedema, vascular collapse, anaphylactic shock) listed with frequency unknown.
adverse_event_history.md: Severe allergic reactions (dyspnoea, angioedema, vascular collapse, anaphylactic shock) listed with frequency unknown.

evidence.claim: A chamomile extract reduced anxiety scores in mild to moderate GAD more than placebo.
evidence.test_article_detail: oral standardised chamomile extract capsules, 8 weeks
evidence.outcome_summary: Greater HAM-A reduction than placebo (57 randomised).

md.claim: A chamomile extract reduced anxiety scores in mild to moderate [GAD](#term:gad) more than [placebo](#term:placebo).

evidence.claim: Continued chamomile extract did not significantly reduce GAD relapse versus placebo.
evidence.test_article_detail: pharmaceutical-grade chamomile extract capsules; 26-week randomised placebo substitution
evidence.outcome_summary: Relapse 15.2 % vs 25.5 % (HR 0.52, p = 0.16); symptoms stayed lower on chamomile (n = 93).

md.claim: Continued chamomile extract did not significantly reduce GAD relapse versus placebo.
md.outcome_summary: Relapse 15.2 % vs 25.5 % (HR 0.52, p = 0.16); symptoms stayed lower on chamomile (n = 93).

evidence.claim: A standardised chamomile extract did not improve sleep in chronic primary insomnia.
evidence.test_article_detail: standardised chamomile extract, 28 days, pilot RCT
evidence.outcome_summary: No significant difference in sleep-diary outcomes (n = 34); NCCIH judges insomnia evidence minimal.
evidence.note: Brief expected 'C'; the one RCT read is null, so the honest summary is 'tested, no benefit shown'.

md.claim: A standardised chamomile extract did not improve sleep in chronic primary insomnia.
md.outcome_summary: No significant difference in sleep-diary outcomes (n = 34); NCCIH judges insomnia evidence minimal.

evidence.claim: Chamomile flower is traditionally used for minor gastrointestinal complaints and mouth, throat and skin inflammations.
evidence.outcome_summary: EMA: 'symptomatic treatment of minor gastro-intestinal complaints such as bloating and minor spasms'.
